title: From first conversation to finished work.
html:
1. Talk with us Tell us what you need and when. We'll help you size the project.
  2. Get matched We find the intern whose skills and interests fit your project best, so you get the right designer and they get the right experience.
  3. Set up the work Paying clients buy a block of hours through the CU Denver storefront. Partnership projects start once the match is set.
  4. Build together Work runs remote and mostly asynchronous, with check-ins by video call. You mentor; we stay with the project.

Where client fees go. They fund the Agency's infrastructure: Articulate 360, Riverside, SEHD Canvas, and the other specialized software our students use to build and host your project.

title: For clients and partners.
html:
What does it cost?

Organizations pay a flat $40 per hour. You buy a block of hours through the CU Denver storefront, and they stay banked until your project uses them. Projects with SEHD faculty and programs, and with Agency alumni who mentor, are free.

Can you host our course or training?

Yes. We host Canvas courses, workshops, and academies and can administer them as your LMS. We host Articulate Rise modules with participation and completion tracking, manage video on YouTube or Wistia, and publish podcasts through Riverside and PodBean to Spotify, Apple Podcasts, and the other major platforms. Take any of it à la carte.

Who does the work?

Graduate students in CU Denver's Learning Design & Technology program, enrolled in the INTE 6930 internship, with you as their client mentor.

What's expected of me as a client?

Mentorship. You share what you need, give feedback, and meet with your intern for check-ins by video call. Most of the work happens asynchronously in between.

title: From application to your first client.
html:
1. Apply Tell us about your skills, your schedule, and what you want to get better at.
  2. Meet with Brad Brad Hinson meets with every student to talk through interests and find the right fit.
  3. Enroll in INTE 6930 The internship course is required. It's where your project work earns credit.
  4. Start your project Meet your client mentor and get to work, remote and mostly asynchronous, with check-ins by video call.

title: Once Agency, always Agency.
custom_excerpt: Our alumni work across higher ed, K-12, corporate, nonprofit, and freelance learning design. When you need help on a project and want to mentor, come back. We'll assign an LDT intern to your project at no cost.
html:
• As a student You learn on real projects, mentored by working professionals, many of them Agency alumni.
  • As a graduate You join the Agency alumni network working across the field.
  • As a mentor You bring us a project. We match you with an intern, free, and you mentor the next designer.

title: For students.
html:
Do I have to enroll in a course?

Yes. INTE 6930 is required to participate. MA students can take it up to 3 times toward the degree; certificate students take it once.

Is this a job?

No. This is not employment. Agency projects are learning experiences, taken for credit.

How are projects assigned?

Brad Hinson meets with every student and every client. We look for a project that builds the skills you're after and a client who needs what you can offer.

How much time does it take?

Projects run part-time and remotely. Most work is asynchronous, with check-ins by video call, so it can fit around a full-time job.

What software will I use?

Whatever the client uses. Agency projects have run on Canvas, Blackboard, Thinkific, Teachable, Circle.so, Articulate Rise and Storyline, Adobe Creative Suite, Riverside.fm, Podbean, YouTube, Ghost, WordPress, Shorthand, and AI tools like ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini. Learning a new platform quickly is part of the job.
